cover.alt: Tansy and Brindle by a fresh hole under the big oak while nuts fly through the air

text: It was the last warm day of fall in Willowbrook Hollow.
Tansy the squirrel had a pile of nuts. It was a big pile. No, it was a HUGE pile.
“One hundred nuts!” said Tansy. “And the frost comes soon. I have to bury them all today!”
She hopped up and down, and the whole pile went clack, clack.

media.alt: Tansy hops beside a huge pile of nuts under a fall tree

text: Tansy had a plan, because Tansy always had a plan. She had scratched it on a scrap of bark.
“Step one: dig holes,” she read. “Step two: drop in the nuts. Step three: make a map. Step four: do not lose the map.”
She looked at the pile. She looked at her two small paws.
“I need help,” she said. “Lots of help. Fast help!”

media.alt: Tansy holds up her plan on a scrap of bark next to her pile of nuts

text: Tansy ran to the stream. Pip and Pebble were fixing a raft.
“Can you help me bury nuts?” asked Tansy.
“We are busy,” said Pip. “The raft has a leak.”
“It does not have a leak,” said Pebble. “It has a hole.”
“A hole IS a leak,” said Pip.
Tansy left them to fuss.

media.alt: Pip and Pebble argue over a raft by the stream while Tansy asks for help

text: Puddle was by the water, looking up at a cloud.
“Puddle, can you help me bury nuts?”
“Not now,” said Puddle. “That cloud looks like a duck. Or a boot. I have to see which.”
Up on the gate, Echo had his eyes shut.
“Echo, can you help me?” asked Tansy.
“Busy napping, Nutty,” said Echo. He did not open his eyes.

media.alt: Puddle stares up at the sky while Echo naps on the gate and Tansy looks between them

text: Wren came zipping by. “Breaking news!” she sang. “Tansy needs help! Tansy needs help!”
“Yes!” said Tansy. “So will you help me?”
“Oh, I can’t,” said Wren. “I have to tell the news. It is VERY big news.”
And off she flew.
Tansy sat down on her nuts. The whole Hollow was busy.

media.alt: Wren zips away singing while Tansy sits glumly on top of her pile of nuts

text: Well, not the WHOLE Hollow.
Under the big oak, in his sunny spot, lay Brindle. The old dog was dozing.
“Brindle?” said Tansy. “Are you busy?”
Brindle opened one eye. He did not answer for a long time.
“I am old,” he said at last. “Old dogs are never busy.”
“So you CAN help!” said Tansy.
“Dogs are good at digging,” said Brindle slowly. “It is what we do.”

media.alt: Brindle dozes in his sunny spot under the big oak as Tansy tiptoes up to him

text: Brindle got up. It took a while. First his front end, then his back end, then his tail.
“Step one: dig holes!” said Tansy. “Go, go, go!”
Brindle dug. Dirt flew out between his back legs. He dug fast for an old dog.
In no time, there was a deep, deep hole.

media.alt: Brindle digs fast, sending dirt flying, while Tansy cheers

text: Tansy dropped in ten nuts, plink, plink, plink.
“Step two: done!” she said. “Next hole, please!”
Brindle began to dig the next hole. But he dug it in the SAME spot.
Dirt flew out. So did the nuts. They went up over his back and over the hill.

media.alt: Brindle digs in the same hole and nuts fly up over his back toward the hill

text: Bonk, bonk, bonk!
“OW!” came a yell from the gate.
“Sorry, Echo!” said Tansy. “Are those my nuts?”
“They WERE your nuts,” said Echo. He rubbed his head. Then he went back to napping.
Brindle looked at the hole. “Hmm,” he said, “dogs are good at digging. We are not so good at stopping.”

media.alt: Nuts bonk Echo on the head as he sits on the gate

text: They went to a new spot. Tansy dug. Brindle dug. Tansy dropped in nuts.
Then Tansy looked up. Brindle was not digging. Brindle was asleep, flat on top of the hole.
“Brindle!” said Tansy. “Wake up! You are on the nuts!”
Brindle just snored. The leaves fell on him, one by one.

media.alt: Brindle sleeps flat on top of the new hole while Tansy tugs at him and leaves fall

text: Tansy did not want to wait. So she found a new spot. It was a soft brown hill of leaves.
It was a very good hill. It was warm. It went up and down, up and down.
She pushed nuts into the hill. Ten, twenty, thirty!
And then the hill gave a big yawn.

media.alt: Tansy pushes nuts into a warm pile of leaves, and a brown ear sticks out of the top

text: The hill stood up. The hill gave a big shake.
Leaves flew and nuts flew, plink, plonk, plunk!
“Oh,” said Tansy, “that hill was you.”
Wren came zipping back. “Breaking news!” she sang. “Brindle ate all of Tansy’s nuts!”
“I did not eat them,” said Brindle.
“Breaking news!” sang Wren. “Brindle did not eat the nuts! He is a hill!”

media.alt: Brindle stands up and shakes, sending leaves and nuts flying, while Wren swoops overhead

text: “We have to do better,” said Tansy. “Step three: make a map!”
She picked up the last of the nuts. She dug a hole all by herself. In went the nuts.
Then she scratched a map on her bark. There was a wavy line for the stream. There was an X for the nuts.
“There,” she said. “Now we can’t lose them.”

media.alt: Tansy proudly holds up her new bark map beside a hole full of nuts

text: She looked at the hole. It was open. Anyone could see the nuts. A crow could take them!
So she put the bark on top, like a lid. Then she put dirt on the bark, pat, pat, pat.
“Step four,” said Tansy. “Do not lose the map.”
She looked at her paws. She looked at the ground. She looked at Brindle.
“Brindle,” she said. “Where is my map?”

media.alt: Tansy pats dirt over a hole, and one corner of her bark map pokes out

text: Brindle looked at the fresh dirt. He gave it a sniff.
“Your map,” he said slowly, “is on your nuts. Under the dirt.”
Tansy flopped down on the grass. “I hid the map!” she said. “I hid the map that tells me where I hid the nuts!”
Brindle nodded. That was the most Tansy thing he had ever seen.

media.alt: Tansy flops flat on the grass in despair while Brindle sniffs the fresh dirt

text: “Let me dig it up,” said Brindle.
He dug and dug. Out came dirt, and then a stick. Out came… a bone.
Brindle’s tail began to wag. “My bone!” he said. “I lost this bone last spring!”
“YOU lose things too?” said Tansy.
“Everyone loses things,” said Brindle. He gave the bone a lick. “Some of us are just slower about it.”

media.alt: Brindle proudly holds up an old muddy bone he dug up while Tansy stares

text: By dusk, Tansy had a bone and a stick. She had a lot of dirt on her tail.
She did not have one nut. Not in a hole. Not on the grass. Not one.
“I lost them all,” she said. “One hundred nuts. Gone.”
Her big tail drooped. Even her ears drooped.

media.alt: At dusk, a sad Tansy sits by empty holes with a bone and a stick beside her

text: Brindle sat down next to her. He sat slowly, the way old dogs do.
“A lost nut is like a nap,” he said. “You can’t get one if you try too hard.”
“What does that mean?” asked Tansy.
“It means it is my turn,” said Brindle. He tapped his nose. “I have an old nose. But it is a good one.”

media.alt: Brindle sits close to Tansy at dusk and taps his nose with a paw

text: Brindle put his nose down and went sniff, sniff, sniff.
He went to the leaves where he had napped. Out of the leaves came five nuts.
He went up the hill and found ten more under a rock.
He sniffed the fresh dirt and dug up the map. The nuts were under it, of course.
He went to the gate. His nose went up, up, up, to Echo’s satchel.

media.alt: Brindle sniffs his way up to the gate, where Echo sits with his satchel

text: “Echo,” said Brindle. “Your bag smells like nuts.”
Echo opened one eye. “Does it? How odd.”
Out of the satchel came nuts. Lots of nuts. Twenty-two nuts!
“I was keeping them safe,” said Echo. “From the rain. And from Wren.”
Tansy gave him a big hug. Echo made a face. But he did not stop her.

media.alt: Nuts spill out of Echo's satchel as Tansy hugs him and Brindle looks on

text: Then Brindle’s nose led them down to the water.
Puddle was still looking at the cloud. He was sitting on a lumpy nest.
“Puddle,” said Tansy. “What are you sitting on?”
Puddle looked down. “Eggs, I think,” he said. “Brown ones. They are very hard eggs.”
They were not eggs. They were nuts. Thirty of them!
“Oh,” said Puddle. “Well. That cloud was a boot, by the way.”

media.alt: Puddle sits on a nest of nuts by the water, and Tansy and Brindle find him

text: Last of all, they went to the raft. Pip and Pebble had fixed it.
Their raft was full of nuts, from end to end.
“Nuts fell on our raft!” said Pip. “They came from the sky!”
“They came over the hill,” said Pebble. “I saw them.”
“You did not,” said Pip. “You were busy.”
“I am ALWAYS busy,” said Pebble. “I still saw them.”

media.alt: Pip and Pebble argue next to their raft, which is heaped with nuts

text: Back under the oak, Tansy made a big pile. She counted. Then she counted again.
“One short!” she said. “We have all of them but one!”
Brindle sniffed the air. He sniffed the grass. He sniffed Tansy.
“I smell it,” he said, with a frown. “But I can’t find it.”

media.alt: Under the oak at dusk, Tansy counts a big pile of nuts while Brindle sniffs the air

text: Brindle sat down to scratch his ear, scritch, scratch, scritch.
Something fell out of his green bandana. It hit the grass with a plop.
It was one small, brown nut.
“It was on you the whole time!” said Tansy.
Brindle looked at the nut. He looked at Tansy. “Well,” he said. “That is the best spot for a nut I ever saw.”

media.alt: A single nut drops out of Brindle's green bandana as Tansy points and laughs

text: This time, they took it slowly. Brindle dug. Tansy dropped in the nuts. No one napped. No one got bonked.
Tansy did not make a map. She did not need one.
Wren zipped by one last time. “Breaking news!” she sang. “Tansy did NOT lose her nuts!”
“Yet,” said Echo, from the gate.

media.alt: Brindle and Tansy bury nuts together while Wren flies by and Echo smirks from the gate

text: Then Tansy scratched a new plan on bark.
“Step one: bury the nuts. Step two: lose the nuts. Step three: ask Brindle.”
She looked up. Brindle was asleep in his sunny spot again. His old bone was under his chin.
Tansy grinned. Some friends are fast. Some friends are busy. And some friends are slow and old, with the best nose around.

media.alt: At dusk Brindle sleeps under the oak with his bone, and Tansy grins beside him holding her new plan
